p: Clear aligners are not always the better option. When we recommend them, when we do not, and why.
We fit more aligners than braces, but we do not think aligners are right for everyone. Here is how we decide.
Mild to moderate crowding, gaps and many bite problems respond well to aligners, especially in adults who want something discreet and are good at wearing them 22 hours a day.

Severe rotations, some complex bites and patients who know they will not wear a removable appliance often do better with fixed braces. We will tell you if that is you, and refer you to a colleague if we think they will do it better.
In our practice the fees are similar. The bigger difference is time in the chair and how much the treatment depends on you.

p: A few small things at home make the first visit far easier. Most of them are about what you say, not what you do.
Children pick up on our nerves long before they have any of their own. The most useful thing you can do before a first visit is keep it ordinary.
Read a picture book about the dentist, play ‘count the teeth’ with a mirror and avoid words like hurt, needle or brave. They plant the idea that there is something to be brave about.
Book a morning slot when they are fresh. Let them sit on your lap if they want to. We will name every tool before we use it and stop before anyone gets bored.
Praise the visit, not the absence of crying. A sticker and a new toothbrush do the rest.

/journal/whitening-shades.description: How white your teeth can get depends on things a shade tab cannot show. A short guide to setting honest expectations.
h1: What the shade guide won’t tell you about whitening
h2: Fillings and crowns do not whiten
Start with an hour, not a sales pitch.
h4: Why our first visit is an hour long
Aligners or braces? An honest comparison
What the shade guide won’t tell you about whitening
p: How white your teeth can get depends on things a shade tab cannot show. A short guide to setting honest expectations.
Whitening adverts love dramatic numbers: eight shades, ten shades, Hollywood white. The truth is that your starting point decides most of the result, and a shade guide only shows the surface.
Teeth look darker as enamel thins and the yellower layer underneath shows through. Whitening lightens stains in the enamel; it cannot change the colour of what lies beneath it.
If you have tooth-coloured work on your front teeth, it will stay the same shade while the natural teeth around it lighten. We plan for that before we start, not after.
We photograph your shade before and after, under the same light, and tell you a realistic range at the consult. Most people land within it.

/treatments/check-ups-and-hygiene.description: A slow, thorough look at your teeth and gums, a careful clean, and a straight answer about what (if anything) needs doing.
h2: Start with an hour, not a sales pitch.
p: A slow, thorough look at your teeth and gums, a careful clean, and a straight answer about what (if anything) needs doing.
Every treatment starts with a $95 consult: a scan, a preview of the result and a written plan with every price. The consult fee comes off the treatment.

We start in an ordinary chair and talk for a few minutes: anything that hurts, anything you have been putting off, anything you would like to change. Then a full exam, a gum check and an oral cancer screen, with X-rays only when they are actually due.
Your hygienist then cleans above and below the gumline and polishes away the surface stains. We use warm water and go gently around sensitive spots.
Most people describe it as a bit odd rather than uncomfortable. If an area is tender, we use numbing gel first. Raise a hand and we stop.
You leave with a short written summary: what we saw, what we cleaned and when to come back. If something needs treatment, it comes with a price before you go.
Every one starts the same way: a consult, a scan and a price in writing.

/about.title: About — Alder Dental
/about.description: A small dental studio on Hawthorne, built around longer appointments, written prices and the same faces every visit.
h2: Ten years of rushed appointments taught us what not to do.
Start with an hour, not a sales pitch.
p: Four clinicians, three treatment rooms and a rule that nobody leaves the chair without understanding what just happened.
Dr. Imogen Vale opened Alder in 2012 after a decade in a city practice where appointments ran to the minute and nobody had time to explain anything.

She wanted the opposite: longer visits, fewer patients and a plan you could take home and read. Fourteen years later the studio is still small on purpose. We see around twenty people a day, and the person who plans your treatment is the person who does it.
Most of our new patients come from someone who was nervous too.
Nothing happens in your mouth that you have not had explained first, in plain words, with a picture.
Every plan comes with every fee. If something changes mid-treatment, we stop and update it before we carry on.
Four clinicians, no locums. The person who planned your treatment is the person who does it.
First visits are an hour and routine visits forty minutes. We would rather run fewer appointments than shorter ones.
Nervous patients who book a second visit.
Hover a portrait to clear the glass, or open a profile to read about each of us.
Three treatment rooms, a waiting room with real chairs and a garden you can see from the dental chair.
